tier_reason: Peer-reviewed USENIX ATC'20 paper whose abstract says SplinterDB beats RocksDB by 6-10x on insertions and 2-2.6x on point queries, matches it on small range queries, and cuts write amplification 2x. The paper names the machine but not the exact Xeon model, compiler, or flags, and its trace-replay harness was not confirmed public, so it is B, not A.

corrections.hardware: Dell PowerEdge R720, 32-core 2.00 GHz Intel Xeon CPU (exact model not named), 256 GiB RAM, 960GiB Intel Optane 905p PCIe 3.0 NVMe SSD, 4096-byte blocks; memory capped at 4GiB via a Linux cgroup (per paper section 6.1)
corrections.workload: YCSB-derived trace replay (load phase and workloads A-F, 24B keys, 100B values and a 1KiB-value set) plus microbenchmarks, on an Optane 905p NVMe SSD with memory limited to about 10% of the dataset size (usually 4GiB), per the USENIX ATC'20 paper 'SplinterDB: Closing the Bandwidth Gap for NVMe Key-Value Stores'.
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from the 2020 peer-reviewed paper against the RocksDB of that time, so the current code and current RocksDB may differ. The paper gives the machine (32-core 2.00 GHz Xeon, Optane 905p) but not the exact CPU model, compiler, or flags. It is not confirmed that the paper's YCSB trace replayer is in the public repo.

notes: The abstract numbers match the record exactly. last_commit was the repo pushed_at date (2026-08-18); the newest commit on main is 2026-07-31. License Apache-2.0, 732 stars, not archived and not a fork, all confirmed.

tier_reason: First-party README claim with no published result tables, hardware, or compiler/flags. The 'Improvements beyond LMDB' section says in-tmpfs CRUD benchmarks show libmdbx 10-20% faster than LMDB, and up to 30% faster with build options that relax runtime checks, reproducible with ioArena 'make bench-quartet'. The '10-100K times' line is an unmeasured assertion about 'particular extreme cases'.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'Up to 30% faster than LMDB in CRUD benchmarks'. In-tmpfs benchmarks that test the engine itself show libmdbx 10-20% faster than LMDB, and up to 30% faster when built with options that downgrade several runtime checks to match LMDB. The README says libmdbx may be slower than LMDB on Windows (LockFileEx locking). A separate comparison bullet asserts 'up to 10-100K times faster than both BoltDB and LMDB in particular extreme cases' (excluding disk I/O), with no data behind it.
corrections.workload: In-tmpfs CRUD benchmarks (engine speed without disk I/O) run with the ioArena harness via 'make bench-quartet', which also covers RocksDB and WiredTiger. No dataset size, key/value sizes, hardware, or result tables are published.
corrections.caveats: Self-reported percentages with no published result tables, hardware, or compiler/flags. The ioArena harness is public (sourcecraft.dev/dqdkfa/ioarena, originally github.com/pmwkaa/ioarena). The README says libmdbx may be slower than LMDB on Windows (LockFileEx) and slower on macOS with the default F_FULLFSYNC durability setting. The '10-100K times faster' line covers unspecified extreme cases and is not a measured figure. Canonical origin is SourceCraft; GitHub Mithril-mine/libmdbx is a mirror.

notes: The measured claim is 10-30% faster than LMDB, not 10-100K x. That line is on the page but is a qualitative extreme-case assertion, so claimed_speedup is rewritten around the CRUD figure. Correct repo_url: the README and libmdbx.dqdkfa.ru name https://sourcecraft.dev/dqdkfa/libmdbx as the origin and https://github.com/Mithril-mine/libmdbx as a mirror (the old github.com/erthink/libmdbx now redirects to Mithril-mine). License Apache-2.0, 1468 stars, last commit 2026-09-25, all confirmed.

tier_reason: The project's own harness (bench/bench.cpp, with bench/rocksdb_support) prints a NuDB vs RocksDB insert/fetch table. The README shows it only as 'a sample output', with no CPU, compiler, or flags for that run, so it is first-party with partial methodology: C.

corrections.caveats: The bench README labels the table 'a sample output', so it is unclear whether it is a captured real run. No CPU model or compiler/flags are given for it; the build instructions use a CMake Release build. The prose cites 340397 ops/sec for fetch at 10M keys, but the table shows 337300. Insert at 10M keys is NA. NuDB is slower than RocksDB on fetch at 100K keys.
